children.objective: In src/nbody_kernel.cu only, explore CTA-level shared-memory tiles of source x, y, z, and mass that are reused by the existing one-thread-per-target mapping. Keep src/launch.json and the baseline target indexing unchanged to isolate source-data reuse. Correctly handle partial source tiles and out-of-range target lanes without bypassing block barriers; preserve self-interaction handling, full output writes, the force law, update order, and exact masses. Do not combine this with warp-per-target mapping or force-math rewrites. Judge candidates using checker results and the official timings at all three sizes; a tile is only a performance hypothesis.
children.subject: Reuse source particles with CTA shared-memory tiling

children.objective: In src/nbody_kernel.cu only, retain baseline indexing, launch configuration, and memory strategy while testing interaction-math changes such as explicit rsqrtf-based reciprocal-distance powers, safe cancellation of the target-mass factor, and modest loop unrolling. Keep float32 semantics within the checker and do not use global fast-math. Preserve softening, self-interaction safety, velocity-before-position update, exact mass copying, and finite output; specifically validate coincident positions, zero/negative dt, and the isolated extreme-mass case. Do not add shared-memory tiling or change the thread-to-target mapping; retain only changes that pass the full checker and improve the official metric.
children.subject: Reduce per-interaction math while preserving float32 correctness

children.objective: Explore a warp-per-target mapping in src/nbody_kernel.cu: lanes cooperatively traverse source indices, accumulate partial force components, and reduce them within the warp. Tune block and items_per_block in src/launch.json together with the kernel's logical output-chunk indexing; ensure the compile-time chunk agrees with the configured grid rule and every target is written exactly once for arbitrary N, including partial warps and small sizes. Keep the baseline force expression and avoid shared-memory staging to isolate this mapping experiment. Preserve all input/output and numerical requirements, then compare correctness and official timings across the three benchmark sizes.
children.subject: Increase source-axis parallelism with warp-cooperative reduction
